decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-31871216) describes a case of well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck with a somatic DPYD exon 11-19 deletion fusion that showed a rapid and sustained response to Fluorouracil and Leucovorin. The claim specifies 'basaloid squamous cell carcinoma' as the disease. The evidence explicitly identifies the tumor as 'well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma', not 'basaloid'. While the molecular profile (DPYD exon 11-19 deletion), therapy (Fluorouracil/Leucovorin), and direction (sensitivity/response) are supported, the specific histological subtype 'basaloid' is not present in the source and is contradicted by the 'well-differentiated' descriptor. Therefore, the claim requires revision to align with the documented pathology. The claim is not fully supported as written (SUPPORTS) nor is it entirely irrelevant (NEI); it is partially supported but factually incorrect regarding the histology, necessitating a REVISIONS verdict.

citations.quote: Pathology evaluation of the resected ulcer (with a right hemimaxillectomy and right-sided neck dissection) identified a 3.5-cm well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma involving the alveolar ridge and maxillary sinus with bone invasion; level I and II (but not III/IV) nodes were involved . . . Based on the findings of the POG analysis, treatment with weekly 5-FU (500 mg/m2) and leucovorin (20 mg/m2) was initiated. an in-frame deletion of exons 11-19 was detected in the genome and transcriptome (Fig. 2).
